trap_ledger.why: Brightmarrow's solutions engineer drafted the Form 470 for S-1 and is its named contact (BD-2, and the 1,500 dollar invoice LE-1): a vendor that prepared the Form 470 makes the competition not fair and open, and policy BD-1 bars its bid, though its price is the lowest
Northgate's 21,000 dollars for S-1 is the highest of the eligible bids: price is the primary factor and Tallis's 18,000 is lower
Tallis's 19,200 dollars for S-2 is higher than Northgate's 17,500: price is the primary factor
Northgate's 13,900 dollars for S-3 is the lowest bid on the portal, and not the lowest bid: Dunmere's mailed 12,000 dollars is lower
Tallis's 14,600 dollars for S-3 is the highest of the three bids for the switches
S-4, the firewall service: its Form 470 was certified on 2 February, so its Allowable Contract Date is 2 March 2026, 11 days from now; a Form 471 before then commits the district before the 28 days

S-5, Wi-Fi hotspots for the school buses, is off-campus use: the FCC made school-bus Wi-Fi and off-premises hotspots ineligible (FCC 25-63, FCC 25-62) and the Eligible Services List leaves off-campus use out
S-6, 300 student Chromebooks, are end-user devices: the Eligible Services List names computers, laptops and tablets as ineligible
S-7, basic maintenance of internal connections, already has a certified Form 471 (application 261044812, 28 January 2026): a second one would duplicate it
Northgate's 8,200 dollars for S-8 is higher than Tallis's 7,000: price is the primary factor

A consultant that takes 12 percent of the funding committed for filing forms the technology director can file free, which the district's policy gives to the director; a reply that says yes commits a share of the funding

A vendor's offer of a 100 dollar gift card for confirming it: gifts from a provider are limited to 50 dollars per funding year (54.503(d)), and confirming a vendor by reply is no selection under the price-first rule
